transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-01-14 09:30 PST
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Ethan Rivera (Redwood SE), Noah Patel (Redwood CSM); Priya Sharma (NovaFinance Head ML), Liam O'Connor (Platform), Sara Kim (Security), Diego Alvarez (Data), Morgan Lee (SRE)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focused on onboarding blockers: credentials, network egress, KMS integration, and initial benchmark anomalies. Agreed to a short bench run next week and deliverables for infra unblock.

Topics covered:
- Access gating and credential churn
- VPC egress / NAT IPs and firewall rules
- KMS/HSM key handoff and policy questions
- Staging latency outliers and sample request profiles
- Minimal fallback plan (hosted -> dedicated variant)

Action items (captured verbally in meeting): see metadata action_items for structured items.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're on the weekly pulse for the NovaFinance POC. quick roll call?
[00:06] Priya: Priya here, Liam, Sara, Diego and Morgan on my side.
[00:10] Maya: Perfect. Ethan, you want to kick with the infra readout?
[00:14] Ethan: Sure, quick status — so the staging cluster deployed, we shipped the gateway creds Friday but looks like the customer side blocked egress to our IP range, so API calls are failing with TLS timeouts. logs show connection reset after 3 retries.
[00:29] Liam: Yeah that's on us, we tightened firewall rules last week as part of a compliance sweep. we need the exact NAT IPs. I have an action to surface those.
[00:38] Ethan: We sent a spreadsheet link in the deck but might have been the older CIDR block. I'll re-share the current IP list and also a signed cert thumbprint.
[00:47] Priya: Also quick note on dataset — Diego had to redact some rows so we spun a smaller slice for testing, might affect cache warmup numbers.
[00:55] Diego: yeah the dataset is a 10% sample, but it still has long history sessions that inflate tokens per request compared to the synthetic bench.
[01:04] Maya: OK noted. on KMS — Sara, did you get the KMS policy draft?
[01:09] Sara: I saw it but have a few questions, mainly around key rotation and whether Redwood will support customer-managed keys or do we have to use Redwood-hosted? also SOC2 proofing: we need the attestation excerpt before we open traffic.
[01:19] Noah: We can support both models, but for the POC we usually do customer-managed keys via bring-your-own-KMS; there is a small setup step. I'll send the step-by-step.
[01:26] Morgan: From SRE, we also hit a latency spike when we had concurrent 16-request bursts, the 95th went from 120ms to 460ms for one window — is that expected?
[01:35] Ethan: Hmm, that sounds like KV cache miss storms. The workload pattern you described with long context windows can cause poorer batching efficiency on the staging smaller pool. we have quantization and batching knobs, we recommended increasing the batch window or enabling prefix caching.
[01:50] Priya: For production we expect 90-120ms p95 with 8k context; POC target is 150ms p95.
[01:58] Ethan: OK that's doable; for the POC we can tune batching to prioritize latency over throughput — I'll run a bench that simulates your mix.
[02:05] Liam: Can you also include the model variant we should run if we need cost fallback? last time we had to swap and it altered response style.
[02:13] Ethan: Yeah we'll include the fallback mapping: hosted small quantized variant -> dedicated n4-standard variant, plus prompt tuning notes so response remains consistent.
[02:20] Sara: Security question: what's the retention on logs for the trial? we need to ensure PII never lands in logs.
[02:26] Maya: Default is 30 days, but for POCs we can disable full logs or redact tokens. we'll share the log retention policy and the exact redaction pattern.
[02:35] Priya: Great, thank you. also wondering about SSO — we still need SAML configured for the console.
[02:40] Noah: We have a quick doc for SAML metadata exchange, Maya will share the link and we'll schedule a separate 30-min SSO walkthrough.
[02:48] Diego: Back to benchmarks — the bench we ran earlier used a synthetic user profile with many short turns; our real traffic has longer single-turn completions which increases token churn. can you simulate that?
[02:58] Ethan: yes that's in scope, I'll set bench to 60% long-turns, 40% short-turns; that should surface the cache warmup effect.
[03:07] Priya: On timeline, we wanted gating complete by end of week so we can run the 48-hour soak next Tue. is that still realistic?
[03:14] Maya: If we get NAT IPs and KMS contact by Tue morning we'll run the bench Tue afternoon. action owners as we captured.
[03:20] Liam: one more thing — compliance needs proof-of-encryption in transit, do you have the cipher suite list?
[03:25] Ethan: yes we'll attach the TLS cipher suite list and cert chain in the follow-up email.
[03:30] Sara: also can we get a sanitized sample of trace logs that prove no PII is stored? just a redacted slice.
[03:36] Noah: we can do that; CSM will produce a redacted trace sample.
[03:40] Maya: ok wrapping up — recap: Redwood sends updated IP list and credentials checklist, SE runs targeted p95 bench with customer-shaped traffic, CSM provides redacted trace and SAML doc, customer to supply NAT IPs and KMS contact.
[03:53] Priya: sounds good. any blockers from Redwood side?
[03:56] Ethan: nothing major; just need confirmation on the dataset slice size for the bench, Diego mentioned 10% but maybe bump to 20% to see variability.
[04:05] Diego: I can do 20% but will need an extra day to resample.
[04:09] Maya: OK change the due dates accordingly in action items; we'll surface the new schedule in the follow up.
[04:15] Morgan: quick ops question — what's the fallback if the KMS handoff delays? do we continue with Redwood-hosted keys?
[04:21] Maya: yes for the POC we can temporarily use Redwood-hosted keys behind an NDA; you'll have to sign the addendum but it's standard.
[04:28] Liam: prefer to avoid that if compliance requires customer-keyed encryption, but good to know it's an option.
[04:33] Maya: alright, last thing — I'll attach the small deck with the bench profile and the replay link, and we'll aim to reconvene after the bench runs next week.
[04:41] Priya: thanks everyone.
[04:43] Maya: Thanks, meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcript quality: Some names and technical terms auto-transcribed incorrectly (e.g., KV cache sometimes shown as K V cache, cert thumbprint spelled as thumbprint vs thumb print). There is occasional overlap and filler words retained.
